title: osewa — faster than ssh, survives like mosh, never garbles
excerpt: The terminal protocol for the age of agents. Your agent runs for hours on the host; check in from a laptop or a phone, on any network, over QUIC or TLS WebSocket.
content_html:
The terminal protocol for the age of agents. Your agent runs for hours on the host; check in from a laptop or a phone, on any network.

$ history

1995 ssh devbox

2012 mosh devbox

2026 osewa attach devbox

$ ▍

▼ PRESS ↓ OR SCROLL TO START

§1 Why nowselect your protocol

ssh and mosh were built for networks we no longer have.

ssh 1995

The session is its TCP connection: it dies when the network changes, and each key waits behind the download.

ROAMING

ECHO / LOAD

FIDELITY

mosh 2012

Survives roaming, but its own emulator can garble your screen. UDP only, no forwards, no scrollback.

ROAMING

ECHO / LOAD

FIDELITY

osewa 2026

The session lives on the host with Ghostty's engine. Forwards and exec share the connection, over QUIC or TCP.

ROAMING

ECHO / LOAD

FIDELITY

On a bad network, keys echo 8–100× faster than ssh.

§5 Quick startLinux and macOS hosts

ssh once. osewa after that.

$ osewa login --service me@devbox # install, enroll, run as a service

$ osewa attach devbox # attach to (or create) a session

$ osewa forward devbox 3000 # forward localhost:3000

$ osewa exec devbox -- make test # run a command, no terminal

$ osewa update devbox # upgrade the host over osewa

On your phone today: Moshi for iOS and Android has osewa as an experimental transport beside mosh. The host needs osewa and moshi-hook.

§7 How it works

Separate the session from the transport. Then make it hard to kill.

01 · HYBRID CARRIER

QUIC and TLS WebSocket, raced on every connect

QUIC gets a 300 ms head start; if UDP is blocked, the WebSocket wins. Nothing to configure.

02 · HOLDER

Connections come and go. The session stays.

One process per session on the host keeps the PTY, the screen and your unacked input.

03 · FLIGHT CONTROL

A download can't bury your echo

Keystrokes go ahead of bulk, and a slow link gets the latest screen, not a backlog.

QUIC · UDP · 1 RTT

TLS WS · TCP · +300 ms

§8 Agentsfinal level

The agent keeps working. You check in when it needs you.
